references.observation: The photograph shows a small charcoal-tiled canopy over two bare timber posts, with a plain tie beam, shallow stone feet and an open walkway between diamond-lattice fence runs.
2026 footage shows the named tea-house façade behind the planting. The gate and the position of its fence are outside the frame.
The 2018 photo shows the Water Village tea-room veranda, sign and window joinery.

The Summer Palace festival photograph shows two red lanterns on the timber gate posts, the diamond-lattice fence and the same grey roof profile seen in the 2017 photograph. The paved approach passes through the gate toward the dark timber tea-room facade. The park’s festival map marks Water Village at the east side of the Farming and Weaving garden.

limitations: The fence extends behind foliage in the photograph. Its hidden end and the canopy dimensions are estimated.

The 2017 and July 2026 photographs agree on the signed approach from the south. The PMTiles south range and the paved approach visible in two aerial versions constrain the placement west of the range midpoint. The nominal 7 m setback remains approximate. The gate and fence ends are partially obscured in the aerial images.
The July photograph shows a festival display. The date range for the lanterns is unknown.
